facts.fact: The Ministry of Economy and Finance says public procurement management is among the SIGFiP module 1 functions developed to date and due to be deployed from early January 2026.

systems.system: SIGFiP (Système Intégré de Gestion des Finances Publiques)

GAB.note: Not stated in service or online tendering; deployment is due January 2026.
Banks and payment operators appear only as partners of the Treasury platform; nothing on the central bank.
Nothing on consumer protection in digital finance.

systems.system: SIGFiP (Système Intégré de Gestion des Finances Publiques)

GAB.note: SIGFiP module 1 (revenue, spending, procurement) is due 15 December 2025 and deployment from January 2026, so it is not stated in use; no paper statement and no architecture stated.
Nothing on government payments to people.
The communique does not say who builds or runs SIGFiP.
Nothing on mobile money or retail payments.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Economy and Finance says SIGFiP will centralise tax, non-tax and customs payments on a single Treasury-backed e-payment platform, with revenue centralisation among the functions due for deployment from January 2026.

GAB.note: Platform is described as being set up; no figure for electronic share.
Revenue centralisation in SIGFiP is a Treasury payment platform; no tax filing system or online filing stated.
